questions.prompt: Why does dynamic power grow roughly with the cube of clock frequency?
options: P = C V² f, and a higher f needs a higher V
questions.explanation: Voltage scales with frequency, and enters squared.

questions.prompt: A memory-bound kernel runs at a lower core clock. What happens?
options: About the same time, less energy
questions.explanation: DRAM sets the time; the core clock only sets the power.

questions.prompt: With the Horowitz 45 nm figures (32-bit DRAM read ≈ 640 pJ, FP32 multiply ≈ 3.7 pJ), roughly how many multiplies cost the same energy as one DRAM read?
Why can a 50 ms benchmark overstate a kernel's speed in a long job?
options: Thermal and power limits take seconds to bite: long runs may throttle

questions.prompt: Which optimisations in this course also save energy?
options: Anything that cuts DRAM traffic (coalescing, tiling, fusion, FlashAttention), and finishing sooner
questions.explanation: Data movement dominates the energy bill.
